prompt:
Iteration 1/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: This initial batch registers twelve scientifically motivated, cell-count adequate contrasts in dependency_composite. The outcome scale is signed so that more negative values mean stronger dependency; for contrasts registered with direction -1, a positive signed estimate indicates a more negative raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast and therefore stronger dependency in the exposed group, whereas a positive signed estimate for tp53_loss with direction +1 indicates higher/less negative composite dependency. The practical threshold is 0.15 absolute composite units. I prioritize known driver, collateral-vulnerability, checkpoint, and metabolic-stress genes with plausible directions: KRAS, EGFR, BRAF, MTAP loss, STK11 loss, KEAP1 loss, PTEN loss, MYC amplification, and MSI-high are expected to increase dependency (more negative composite), with MTAP loss especially motivated by known collateral PRMT5/MAT2A vulnerabilities and KEAP1/STK11 losses by metabolic and oxidative-stress dependencies. TP53 loss is hypothesized in the opposite direction because checkpoint/apoptotic-pathway loss may reduce reliance on selected dependency pathways. Lung adenocarcinoma versus squamous is included as a lineage-level context, expecting adenocarcinoma to show stronger dependency but acknowledging plausible squamous-specific lineage dependencies. research_marker_e is included as a binary constructed assay; because it has no assigned biological role, the hypothesis is exploratory: positivity may mark increased dependency if the assay was constructed to capture vulnerability, but no association or an opposite association is a plausible alternative. These tests are associations within this dataset only, not causal claims. Future work will prioritize interactions or subgroup follow-ups only if a main contrast crosses the 0.15 threshold with reasonably tight uncertainty, especially for marker-mutation or mutation-pathway interactions.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect

Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. expectation

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: Selecting all twelve pre-registered discovery contrasts. These cover the highest-value initial set: a lineage-subtype contrast, canonical driver and collateral-vulnerability alterations (MTAP, KRAS, EGFR, BRAF, MYC), tumor suppressor/pathway losses (STK11, KEAP1, PTEN, TP53), MSI-high, and the exploratory research marker. For all direction -1 claims, positive returned signed estimates mean the exposed group has a lower/more-negative raw dependency_composite, i.e., stronger dependency relative to comparator. For H11 (TP53 loss, direction +1), positive signed estimates mean higher/less-negative raw composite, consistent with weaker measured dependency. Each contrast is adequately powered in principle, and all comparisons have sufficient group counts in the supplied variables. No validation or reassessment is requested because no evidence exists yet; the purpose is to estimate 95% Welch intervals and compare signed effects to the 0.15-unit scientific threshold.

prompt:
Iteration 1/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The discovery batch shows that most pre-registered drivers and subgroups do not show meaningful main effects on dependency_composite, but three signals are informative after accounting for the already-signed scale. For claims registered with direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a lower/more-negative raw dependency score, i.e. stronger measured dependency; for H11 direction +1, a positive signed estimate means a higher/less-negative raw score. H10 (MSI-high, signed +0.775; 95% CI +0.664 to +0.885) is a large association in the claimed direction and is accepted as a meaningful discovery in this dataset. H11 (TP53 loss, signed +0.829; CI +0.767 to +0.891) is also large, in the claimed direction, and accepted. These are associations within this supplied dataset, not causal or generalizable conclusions. H8 (PTEN loss, signed +0.239; CI +0.145 to +0.332) is promising but borderline: the point estimate exceeds the 0.15-unit threshold, but the lower bound is just below it, and the 12-test discovery screen makes a marginal effect worth independent confirmation before acceptance. I therefore mark H8 unresolved and request validation. H7 (KEAP1 loss) is confidently opposite to the pre-registered hypothesis: signed -0.810 means the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is positive by about 0.81 units, i.e. KEAP1-loss lines have weaker measured composite dependency. The original H7 direction is rejected and closed, but the reversed hypothesis is biologically interesting and should be formalized as a new claim. EGFR amplification is also not accepted: its signed estimate is slightly opposite, and its interval does not establish a robust threshold-crossing opposite effect. H5 (MTAP loss), H2 KRAS, H6 STK11, H9 MYC, H4 BRAF, H1 adenocarcinoma versus squamous, and H12 marker_e have intervals concentrated near zero or sub-threshold, so they are rejected for the pre-registered main contrasts. Critical checks now should target robustness and confounding: whether TP53 and MSI effects persist when stratified by the other strong variable, whether TP53 persists by library, whether lineage subtypes reproduce the MSI and TP53 effects, and whether the reversed KEAP1 signal is reproducible as a formal opposite-direction claim. The strong effects could still reflect dataset construction or correlation among measured features; validation and stratified follow-up are therefore warranted before any stronger interpretation.

prompt:
Iteration 1/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: Synthesis of the current evidence supports four dataset-level associations with dependency_composite. PTEN loss is now accepted as associated with stronger measured dependency: the discovery signed estimate was +0.239 composite units (95% CI +0.145 to +0.332) for the pre-registered direction of greater dependency, and independent validation gave a larger signed estimate of +0.294 (independent lower bound approximately +0.149, upper +0.439). The independent lower bound is essentially at the 0.15-unit threshold, but the discovery point and interval plus the independent point estimate jointly make a meaningful positive effect more plausible than a null or sub-threshold effect; I accept it as a robust association in this supplied dataset, not as causal evidence or a claim of broad generalizability. MSI-high is accepted as associated with markedly stronger dependency: signed +0.775 (95% CI +0.664 to +0.885). TP53 loss is accepted as associated with weaker measured dependency/higher composite scores: signed +0.829 under the +1-direction claim (95% CI +0.767 to +0.891). record.narrative: The next discovery set focuses on whether the four accepted supplied-dataset signals are mutually confounded or robust across genomic and technical backgrounds, and on whether previously null alterations become meaningful in informative co-mutation strata. For claims registered with direction -1, positive signed estimates correspond to stronger dependency in the exposed group relative to comparator; for claims registered with direction +1, positive signed estimates correspond to higher/less-negative composite scores, i.e. weaker measured dependency. I propose four main-strata robustness contrasts: TP53 loss among KEAP1-intact cells; KEAP1 loss among TP53-intact and MSI-negative cells; MSI-high among TP53-intact and KEAP1-intact cells; and PTEN loss among KEAP1-intact cells. These tests ask whether each effect is an independent marker association or is largely carried by co-occurring accepted variables. I also propose formal interaction contrasts: whether the TP53-loss effect is larger in MSI-negative cells than MSI-high cells; whether the MSI-high effect is larger in TP53-intact cells than TP53-loss cells; whether the KEAP1-loss effect is larger in TP53-intact cells than TP53-loss cells; and whether the PTEN-loss effect is larger in PIK3CA-mutant cells? The registered direction is that PTEN effect is stronger in PIK3CA wild-type cells, consistent with PIK3CA mutation potentially masking PTEN vulnerability. For all interactions, raw estimates are exposed-comparator in the named subgroup minus the complement, then signed to the claim direction. If interaction estimates are near zero, the accepted effects are approximately additive across backgrounds; if they are threshold-crossing, the effects are context-dependent. I additionally propose three technical-background robustness checks restricted to the Avana library, which contains most lines, to see whether MSI-high, KEAP1 loss, and PTEN loss remain associated with dependency_composite in the dominant screen technology/background. Finally, I propose a follow-up for STK11 loss in KEAP1-intact cells. STK11 was null overall, but KEAP1 co-loss could mask a dependency effect; if STK11 loss shows stronger dependency only when KEAP1 is intact, that would refine the interpretation. Plausible alternatives remain important: accepted large effects could be driven by correlated genomic features or dataset construction; interactions could be null because the variables mark the same biological axis; technical-library restrictions could reduce effective sample size; STK11 could remain null even within KEAP1-intact strata. These are still associations in the supplied dataset, not causal claims.

prompt:
Iteration 2/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: Selecting twelve follow-up analyses that test whether the currently accepted supplied-dataset associations are robust to mutual co-occurrence and technical library background, rather than expanding broadly to new predictors. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means higher/less-negative composite dependency, i.e. weaker measured dependency. H14 and H15 test TP53 loss and MSI-high in each other's absence. H24 and H25 test KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss in each other's absence, while H26 and H27 test KEAP1 and MSI-high in strata that are both TP53-intact and MSI-negative or TP53/KEAP1-intact, respectively; these are the strongest direct checks for confounding among the large accepted markers. H22 and H28 test PTEN loss in TP53-intact and KEAP1-intact strata to see whether the smaller PTEN effect survives removal of the major accepted co-occurring variables. H19, H33, H34, and H35 restrict each accepted marker to the dominant Avana CRISPR library background, testing whether the associations are not simply artifacts of library imbalance. If these effects remain above the 0.15-unit threshold in clean strata and intervals are reasonably informative, I will treat the accepted markers as robust dataset-level associations. If some effects attenuate sharply, I will interpret the original accepted markers as partly context-dependent or confounded by correlated measured features rather than independent associations. No validation is requested at this stage; these are discovery analyses intended to sharpen the current claim set.

Iteration 2/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: The new discovery batch supports robustness of the four current supplied-dataset associations, especially for the large TP53-loss, MSI-high, and KEAP1-loss signals. Estimates are already signed to claim direction: positive signed estimates for +1 claims mean higher/less-negative composite dependency, while positive signed estimates for -1 claims mean stronger dependency. TP53-loss remains large in MSI-negative cells (R14 +0.823, CI +0.762 to +0.884), in KEAP1-intact cells (R19 +0.800, CI +0.744 to +0.857), and within Avana-library cells (R16 +0.830, CI +0.765 to +0.896). MSI-high remains large in TP53-intact cells (R15 +0.761, CI +0.656 to +0.865), in TP53/KEAP1-intact cells (R21 +0.766, CI +0.667 to +0.866), and in Avana cells (R23 +0.784, CI +0.668 to +0.901). KEAP1-loss remains large when TP53-intact (R18 +0.780, CI +0.719 to +0.841), in TP53-intact and MSI-negative cells (R20 +0.805, CI +0.750 to +0.860), and in Avana cells (R24 +0.801, CI +0.731 to +0.871). These patterns argue that the large associations are not explained simply by co-occurrence with another accepted marker or by the dominant library background. PTEN-loss is more modest but remains above threshold across TP53-intact (R17 +0.259, CI +0.169 to +0.349), KEAP1-intact (R22 +0.250, CI +0.156 to +0.345), and Avana-restricted (R25 +0.251, CI +0.151 to +0.351) strata. The PTEN robustness intervals have lower bounds only slightly above the 0.15-unit threshold for H28 and H35, so PTEN acceptance remains conditional on treating it as a moderate, internally replicated supplied-dataset association rather than a large or independently generalizable effect. Interpret all accepted effects as dataset-level associations only.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The next discovery set focuses on whether the four accepted supplied-dataset signals are mutually confounded or robust across genomic and technical backgrounds, and on whether previously null alterations become meaningful in informative co-mutation strata. For claims registered with direction -1, positive signed estimates correspond to stronger dependency in the exposed group relative to comparator; for claims registered with direction +1, positive signed estimates correspond to higher/less-negative composite scores, i.e. weaker measured dependency. I propose four main-strata robustness contrasts: TP53 loss among KEAP1-intact cells; KEAP1 loss among TP53-intact and MSI-negative cells; MSI-high among TP53-intact and KEAP1-intact cells; and PTEN loss among KEAP1-intact cells. These tests ask whether each effect is an independent marker association or is largely carried by co-occurring accepted variables. I also propose formal interaction contrasts: whether the TP53-loss effect is larger in MSI-negative cells than MSI-high cells; whether the MSI-high effect is larger in TP53-intact cells than TP53-loss cells; whether the KEAP1-loss effect is larger in TP53-intact cells than TP53-loss cells; and whether the PTEN-loss effect is larger in PIK3CA-mutant cells? The registered direction is that PTEN effect is stronger in PIK3CA wild-type cells, consistent with PIK3CA mutation potentially masking PTEN vulnerability. For all interactions, raw estimates are exposed-comparator in the named subgroup minus the complement, then signed to the claim direction. If interaction estimates are near zero, the accepted effects are approximately additive across backgrounds; if they are threshold-crossing, the effects are context-dependent. I additionally propose three technical-background robustness checks restricted to the Avana library, which contains most lines, to see whether MSI-high, KEAP1 loss, and PTEN loss remain associated with dependency_composite in the dominant screen technology/background. Finally, I propose a follow-up for STK11 loss in KEAP1-intact cells. STK11 was null overall, but KEAP1 co-loss could mask a dependency effect; if STK11 loss shows stronger dependency only when KEAP1 is intact, that would refine the interpretation. Plausible alternatives remain important: accepted large effects could be driven by correlated genomic features or dataset construction; interactions could be null because the variables mark the same biological axis; technical-library restrictions could reduce effective sample size; STK11 could remain null even within KEAP1-intact strata. H14 and H15 test TP53 loss and MSI-high in each other's absence. H24 and H25 test KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss in each other's absence, while H26 and H27 test KEAP1 and MSI-high in strata that are both TP53-intact and MSI-negative or TP53/KEAP1-intact, respectively; these are the strongest direct checks for confounding among the large accepted markers. H22 and H28 test PTEN loss in TP53-intact and KEAP1-intact strata to see whether the smaller PTEN effect survives removal of the major accepted co-occurring variables. H19, H33, H34, and H35 restrict each accepted marker to the dominant Avana CRISPR library background, testing whether the associations are not simply artifacts of library imbalance. If these effects remain above the 0.15-unit threshold in clean strata and intervals are reasonably informative, I will treat the accepted markers as robust dataset-level associations. No validation is requested at this stage; these are discovery analyses intended to sharpen the current claim set.","appraise":"The new discovery batch supports robustness of the four current supplied-dataset associations, especially for the large TP53-loss, MSI-high, and KEAP1-loss signals. TP53-loss remains large in MSI-negative cells (R14 +0.823, CI +0.762 to +0.884), in KEAP1-intact cells (R19 +0.800, CI +0.744 to +0.857), and within Avana-library cells (R16 +0.830, CI +0.765 to +0.896). MSI-high remains large in TP53-intact cells (R15 +0.761, CI +0.656 to +0.865), in TP53/KEAP1-intact cells (R21 +0.766, CI +0.667 to +0.866), and in Avana cells (R23 +0.784, CI +0.668 to +0.901). KEAP1-loss remains large when TP53-intact (R18 +0.780, CI +0.719 to +0.841), in TP53-intact and MSI-negative cells (R20 +0.805, CI +0.750 to +0.860), and in Avana cells (R24 +0.801, CI +0.731 to +0.871). These patterns argue that the large associations are not explained simply by co-occurrence with another accepted marker or by the dominant library background. PTEN-loss is more modest but remains above threshold across TP53-intact (R17 +0.259, CI +0.169 to +0.349), KEAP1-intact (R22 +0.250, CI +0.156 to +0.345), and Avana-restricted (R25 +0.251, CI +0.151 to +0.351) strata. prompt:
Iteration 3/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

record.narrative: The current accepted markers are MSI-high, TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, and PTEN loss, all internally robust to some mutual co-occurrence and the dominant Avana library. The next highest-value science is not merely to retest these markers, but to test whether additional measured predictors contribute beyond the large accepted signals and whether the accepted effects are context-dependent. I therefore defer several lower-priority pending lineage-specific checks and the PTEN-PIK3CA main contrast: lineage subtype did not show a main effect, the accepted marker effects are already large and robust across other backgrounds, and the registered PIK3CA interaction H32 is a more direct context test than H23. For new proposals, I test CDKN2A loss and RB1 loss as checkpoint/cell-cycle predictors expected to associate with weaker measured dependency, i.e. higher composite scores, while conditioning on TP53-loss-negative, KEAP1-loss-negative, and MSI-negative cells. This addresses the plausible alternative that any checkpoint-loss association is carried by co-occurring TP53 or KEAP1 loss. I also test ARID1A loss and SMARCA4 loss as chromatin-remodeling predictors expected to create stronger measured dependency, i.e. more negative composite scores, in the same accepted-marker-free stratum. This tests the alternative that chromatin remodeling loss marks a vulnerability axis rather than the checkpoint axis captured by TP53/KEAP1. Finally, I test a TP53-loss interaction with screen_batch in batch_a, because a large measured association could be amplified by technical batch structure. The anticipated direction for the batch interaction is uncertain; a near-zero interaction would support robustness across batches, whereas a threshold-crossing interaction would require reinterpreting TP53-loss as batch-sensitive. Direction convention remains as before: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means higher/less-negative composite scores, i.e. weaker measured dependency. All effects remain supplied-dataset associations unless validated and not causal claims.

Iteration 3/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence

All conclusions remain dataset-level associations only.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"The current accepted markers are MSI-high, TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, and PTEN loss, all internally robust to some mutual co-occurrence and the dominant Avana library. The next highest-value science is not merely to retest these markers, but to test whether additional measured predictors contribute beyond the large accepted signals and whether the accepted effects are context-dependent. I therefore defer several lower-priority pending lineage-specific checks and the PTEN-PIK3CA main contrast: lineage subtype did not show a main effect, the accepted marker effects are already large and robust across other backgrounds, and the registered PIK3CA interaction H32 is a more direct context test than H23. For new proposals, I test CDKN2A loss and RB1 loss as checkpoint/cell-cycle predictors expected to associate with weaker measured dependency, i.e. higher composite scores, while conditioning on TP53-loss-negative, KEAP1-loss-negative, and MSI-negative cells. This addresses the plausible alternative that any checkpoint-loss association is carried by co-occurring TP53 or KEAP1 loss. I also test ARID1A loss and SMARCA4 loss as chromatin-remodeling predictors expected to create stronger measured dependency, i.e. more negative composite scores, in the same accepted-marker-free stratum. This tests the alternative that chromatin remodeling loss marks a vulnerability axis rather than the checkpoint axis captured by TP53/KEAP1. Finally, I test a TP53-loss interaction with screen_batch in batch_a, because a large measured association could be amplified by technical batch structure. The anticipated direction for the batch interaction is uncertain; a near-zero interaction would support robustness across batches, whereas a threshold-crossing interaction would require reinterpreting TP53-loss as batch-sensitive. Direction convention remains as before: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means higher/less-negative composite scores, i.e. weaker measured dependency. H14 and H15 test TP53 loss and MSI-high in each other's absence. H24 and H25 test KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss in each other's absence, while H26 and H27 test KEAP1 and MSI-high in strata that are both TP53-intact and MSI-negative or TP53/KEAP1-intact, respectively; these are the strongest direct checks for confounding among the large accepted markers. H22 and H28 test PTEN loss in TP53-intact and KEAP1-intact strata to see whether the smaller PTEN effect survives removal of the major accepted co-occurring variables. H19, H33, H34, and H35 restrict each accepted marker to the dominant Avana CRISPR library background, testing whether the associations are not simply artifacts of library imbalance. If these effects remain above the 0.15-unit threshold in clean strata and intervals are reasonably informative, I will treat the accepted markers as robust dataset-level associations. If some effects attenuate sharply, I will interpret the original accepted markers as partly context-dependent or confounded by correlated measured features rather than independent associations. TP53-loss remains large in MSI-negative cells (R14 +0.823, CI +0.762 to +0.884), in KEAP1-intact cells (R19 +0.800, CI +0.744 to +0.857), and within Avana-library cells (R16 +0.830, CI +0.765 to +0.896). MSI-high remains large in TP53-intact cells (R15 +0.761, CI +0.656 to +0.865), in TP53/KEAP1-intact cells (R21 +0.766, CI +0.667 to +0.866), and in Avana cells (R23 +0.784, CI +0.668 to +0.901). KEAP1-loss remains large when TP53-intact (R18 +0.780, CI +0.719 to +0.841), in TP53-intact and MSI-negative cells (R20 +0.805, CI +0.750 to +0.860), and in Avana cells (R24 +0.801, CI +0.731 to +0.871). These patterns argue that the large associations are not explained simply by co-occurrence with another accepted marker or by the dominant library background.
