record.narrative: No assessments are due. I register five focused dataset-level comparisons using the signed convention that a positive signed estimate for direction -1 means the exposed group has a lower raw composite dependency_composite, i.e. stronger measured dependency, while direction +1 would mean a higher raw composite, i.e. weaker dependency. The first two proposals target the most persistent unresolved predictor, CDKN2A loss. H1 broadens the search slightly from core-marker-negative comparisons by removing only the two strongest positive-dependency markers, MSI-high and SMARCA4 loss, while keeping TP53 and KEAP1 backgrounds; the expected direction is still raw CDKN2A negative, or positive signed, if CDKN2A has an association not fully confounded by these dominant positive markers. H2 tests the same CDKN2A exposure in an especially clean background: MSI/SMARCA4/TP53/KEAP1 negative, PTEN wild-type, and copy_number_9p21 not deeply deleted. This tests whether the repeated borderline CDKN2A signal can persist when PTEN, dominant positive markers, opposite TP53/KEAP1 markers, and local 9p21 deletion confounding are jointly removed. The plausible alternative is that CDKN2A is a weak, context-limited, or marker-confounded signal rather than an independent threshold-level predictor. H3 tests editing-quality dependence with a formal interaction: if CDKN2A knockout effects require good Cas9 editing, the raw CDKN2A effect should be more negative in high cas9_activity_score than in the complement, giving a negative raw interaction and a positive signed estimate for direction -1. The alternative is null or editing-independent if prior CDKN2A associations are artifacts or context-independent noise. H4 refines the unresolved PTEN high-AXL comparison by requiring absence of MSI-high and SMARCA4 loss; this asks whether the high-AXL PTEN signal is a robust context-specific PTEN association or was partly carried by dominant positive markers. The expected PTEN direction remains stronger measured dependency, but a null or attenuated result would favor a more general PTEN effect without high-AXL specificity. H5 tests PTEN loss under lower editing quality, cas9_activity_score <= 0.9. PTEN has robust accepted evidence overall and in high editing, so this tests robustness of a moderate signal outside high-quality editing. If it remains above threshold, the PTEN association is less editing-dependent; if not, some PTEN evidence may be weaker in lower-quality contexts. These proposals deliberately avoid previously failed CDKN2A high-MYC, high-TMB, and validated high-aneuploidy contexts. All conclusions are associations within this supplied dataset only and do not establish causality, biological mechanism, interpretation of constructed assays, or external generalizability.

The priority is CDKN2A loss, the main unresolved predictor after the core marker map and validation. H169 tests CDKN2A after removing MSI-high and SMARCA4 loss, which have the strongest threshold-level positive dependency signals; H170 tests a very clean background by removing TP53, KEAP1, MSI, SMARCA4, and PTEN and by excluding deep 9p21 deletion, to ask whether CDKN2A retains a threshold-level association independent of dominant markers and local 9p21 confounding. H171 tests editing-quality effect modification via interaction with cas9_activity_score ge 1.0. H165-H167 test CDKN2A in high aneuploidy, high hypoxia, and high EMT restricted to TP53/KEAP1/MSI/SMARCA4-negative cells; H165 is distinct from the broad validated-negative high-aneuploidy test because it is restricted to the core-negative population, but it remains exploratory and is interpreted with caution. The PTEN selections target remaining context boundaries: H172 tests high rnaseq_AXL after removing MSI-high and SMARCA4 loss, H168 tests the same high-AXL PTEN contrast after also requiring TP53/KEAP1-negative status, and H173 tests PTEN under lower Cas9 editing quality. H148-H150 add three core-axis robustness checks in high hypoxia: KEAP1 loss and TP53 loss are direction +1 because their accepted main effect is weaker measured dependency, while SMARCA4 loss is direction -1 because its accepted main effect is stronger measured dependency. For direction -1 claims a positive signed estimate means stronger measured dependency in exposed cells; for direction +1 claims a positive signed estimate means weaker measured dependency. The 0.15-unit threshold will be assessed jointly with uncertainty and any available validation. These are dataset-level associations only; they do not establish causality, mechanism, assay interpretation, or generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 13/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

The hypothesis was stronger measured dependency with PTEN loss. The discovery estimate was +0.299, with a 95% interval from +0.121 to +0.478, and independent validation was also large and direction-consistent: +0.289, with a stringent validation interval from +0.000 to +0.578. The validation lower bound does not clear the 0.15-unit threshold, but it excludes zero under a conservative validation interval, and the two estimates agree closely around a moderate-to-large effect. I therefore accept H116 as a dataset-level context-specific association, while noting that the exact magnitude and context boundary remain uncertain. H158 tested CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A wild type in high aneuploidy. The discovery evidence was borderline but positive: +0.283, 95% interval +0.118 to +0.449. The new independent validation was much smaller and non-supportive: +0.048, with a conservative interval from -0.184 to +0.280. The validation point estimate is below the scientific threshold, and the interval includes zero and substantial effects both below and slightly above threshold. The best available evidence does not corroborate the original claim. I reject H158 as not supported for a threshold-level association in this dataset, and close it. This is a failure to support the registered claim, not proof that CDKN2A loss has no effect in any context or population. I also close H140 as a duplicate untested comparison of CDKN2A loss in high cas9_activity_score because H142 contains the same registered comparison and remains active. Broader synthesis: the core marker map remains the strongest and most reproducible signal in this dataset. MSI-high status and SMARCA4 loss are associated with substantially stronger measured dependency, with validated estimates around +0.79 to +0.83 signed units for the main SMARCA4 and MSI comparisons. TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are associated with weaker measured dependency, with main and validated estimates around +0.77 to +0.84 signed units in the claimed direction. record.narrative: I use the signed convention: direction -1 positive estimates mean stronger measured dependency in the exposed group; direction +1 positive estimates mean weaker measured dependency. The threshold is 0.15 composite units in the claimed direction. H148, H149, and H150 are high-hypoxia robustness checks for KEAP1 loss, SMARCA4 loss, and TP53 loss. Their signed effects are very large, far above threshold, and precise: H148 +0.839 (0.718, 0.960), H149 +0.861 (0.748, 0.974), H150 +0.894 (0.783, 1.005). I accept these as dataset-level context robustness results and close them. They do not establish hypoxia-specific effect modification because no interaction was tested. H173 tests PTEN loss under lower Cas9 quality. The signed estimate is +0.225 with interval +0.038 to +0.412: the point exceeds threshold and excludes zero, so I accept it as a moderate PTEN association in lower editing quality, while noting the interval is wide and the magnitude is imprecise. This is consistent with the broader validated PTEN pattern and argues against PTEN requiring high Cas9 quality, but it is only dataset-level association. CDKN2A remains uncertain. H169 in MSI/SMARCA4-negative cells has point +0.145, below threshold despite excluding zero, so it is deferred. H166 and H167, high hypoxia and high EMT core-negative contexts, have point estimates above threshold but wide intervals and small cells; they are deferred, not accepted. H171 is a formal editing-quality interaction: signed estimate -0.196 (-0.349, -0.042), opposite the claimed direction. I reject the registered interaction; an exploratory inverse interaction is not claimed and is not sufficient to reinterpret without validation. H170 was not evaluable because the exposed cell had only 14 observations, so it remains unresolved and closed. H165 is the strongest new CDKN2A context: high aneuploidy restricted to TP53/KEAP1/MSI/SMARCA4-negative cells, +0.271 (0.146, 0.397). This is above threshold in point estimate and nearly clears threshold at the lower bound, but exposed n=49 and prior broad high-aneuploidy CDKN2A failed independent validation. I keep it unresolved and request validation. For PTEN high AXL, H172 excluding MSI/SMARCA4 gives +0.088 (-0.089, 0.266), which does not support high-AXL-specific PTEN; H168 excluding TP53/KEAP1 also gives +0.183 (0.017, 0.348) but with only 24 exposed observations. These high-AXL context claims remain unresolved and deferred; they do not undermine the broader accepted PTEN-loss association. Overall, the core marker robustness is strong, PTEN remains broadly supported including lower editing quality, and CDKN2A is the main remaining uncertain axis pending validation of H165. All conclusions are dataset-level associations only and do not establish causality, mechanism, biological interpretation of constructed assays, or external generalizability.

The validation lower bound does not clear the 0.15-unit threshold, but it excludes zero under a conservative validation interval, and the two estimates agree closely around a moderate-to-large effect. I therefore accept H116 as a dataset-level context-specific association, while noting that the exact magnitude and context boundary remain uncertain. H158 tested CDKN2A loss versus CDKN2A wild type in high aneuploidy. The discovery evidence was borderline but positive: +0.283, 95% interval +0.118 to +0.449. The new independent validation was much smaller and non-supportive: +0.048, with a conservative interval from -0.184 to +0.280. The validation point estimate is below the scientific threshold, and the interval includes zero and substantial effects both below and slightly above threshold. The best available evidence does not corroborate the original claim. I reject H158 as not supported for a threshold-level association in this dataset, and close it. This is a failure to support the registered claim, not proof that CDKN2A loss has no effect in any context or population. I also close H140 as a duplicate untested comparison of CDKN2A loss in high cas9_activity_score because H142 contains the same registered comparison and remains active. MSI-high status and SMARCA4 loss are associated with substantially stronger measured dependency, with validated estimates around +0.79 to +0.83 signed units for the main SMARCA4 and MSI comparisons. TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are associated with weaker measured dependency, with main and validated estimates around +0.77 to +0.84 signed units in the claimed direction. record.narrative: Due assessments were reassessed with the signed convention: direction -1 positive means stronger measured dependency in exposed versus comparator; direction +1 positive means weaker measured dependency. The threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction. H127 tested CDKN2A loss in a high rnaseq_MYC_log2_tpm context. The validation evidence was direction-consistent but small and imprecise, with a point estimate below threshold and a conservative interval crossing zero. Combined evidence does not support a threshold-level CDKN2A effect in this context; H127 remains rejected and closed. H165 tested CDKN2A loss in high aneuploidy restricted to TP53/KEAP1/MSI/SMARCA4-negative cells. Discovery was relatively positive, around +0.271 with lower bound near threshold, but independent validation was +0.085 with a conservative interval from about -0.055 to +0.225. The validation point estimate is below threshold and does not exclude zero. I therefore reject H165 and close it. This is a failure to support the registered claim, not proof that CDKN2A loss has no effect in any context or population. Together with the previously validated-negative broad high-aneuploidy CDKN2A claim and the now validated-negative high-MYC CDKN2A claim, CDKN2A no longer has robust dataset-level threshold support despite repeated borderline conditional signals. Final scientific report: supported findings are dataset-level associations. SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high status are strongly associated with stronger measured dependency, with main signed estimates near +0.78 to +0.81 and independent validation near +0.80 to +0.83. TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are strongly associated with weaker measured dependency, with main and validated signed estimates near +0.77 to +0.84 in the claimed direction. PTEN loss is moderately associated with stronger measured dependency, with main discovery +0.239 and validation +0.294, plus accepted context-specific support including high MYC and lower Cas9 quality. Negative or unsupported findings include lineage subtype, KRAS mutation, EGFR amplification, BRAF V600E, MTAP loss, STK11 loss, MYC amplification, research markers D/E/F, sex, media-serum contrasts, screen batch, library or omics availability contrasts, and most formal interactions. Effect modification by the tested MYC, AXL, hypoxia, EMT, research-signature, mutation-burden, aneuploidy, Cas9-quality, and subtype contexts has not been established. Unresolved uncertainty is concentrated in PTEN high-AXL boundary tests and residual CDKN2A context signals. PTEN main evidence remains broad and robust, while high-AXL estimates remain imprecise and context-dependent. CDKN2A has multiple near-threshold or above-point estimates, but independent validation has failed to corroborate the most plausible contexts. The most informative next analyses are PTEN loss in high aneuploidy, both as a main effect and as an interaction test, to determine whether the robust PTEN signal survives this genomic-background context and whether high aneuploidy modifies it, and CDKN2A loss in cells without deep 9p21 deletion to test whether any CDKN2A signal persists outside 9p21-deleted backgrounds. If these remain below threshold or non-confirmatory, CDKN2A should be treated as weak or non-robust in this dataset, and PTEN should be summarized as a broad rather than context-specific association. All conclusions are dataset-level associations only; they do not establish causality, biological mechanism, interpretation of constructed assays, or external generalizability.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

Iteration 14/25, stage explore, attempt 2.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: I reassess H7 because its signed discovery and validation evidence are strongly opposite the registered negative-direction claim for KEAP1 loss; KEAP1 loss is better represented by the positive-direction claim H13, so H7 is rejected to keep the accepted claim set coherent. For new comparisons, I use the signed convention: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate supports stronger measured dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate supports weaker measured dependency. The threshold remains 0.15 composite units. The proposals target the main remaining boundaries. PTEN has broad robust support but unresolved context dependence, so I test high-aneuploidy PTEN in a core-marker-negative background and test broad PTEN high-aneuploidy effect modification. I also test high-aneuploidy robustness for SMARCA4, TP53, KEAP1, and MSI-high, plus a SMARCA4 high-aneuploidy interaction, to determine whether the dominant effects are stable in a high genomic-instability background. CDKN2A remains non-robust after validation failures; I test reduced-marker high-EMT and high-hypoxia contexts and a cleaner non-deep-9p21 core-negative context to determine whether any threshold-level signal remains after excluding the largest positive-dependency markers and possible local deletion confounding. I also refine the uncertain PTEN high-AXL boundary by requiring high Cas9 quality. No validation requests are currently available, so these are discovery-stage comparisons. All conclusions remain dataset-level associations only and do not establish causality, mechanism, biological interpretation of constructed assays, or generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 14/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due, and no new proposals are needed for this analysis pass because the key target hypotheses are already registered. I selected 12 active, previously registered comparisons that have no direct discovery evidence and that most directly advance the current decision points. The signed convention remains: for direction -1, a positive signed mean_difference or interaction estimate means stronger measured dependency in the exposed/grouping contrast; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker measured dependency. The outcome-specific meaningful threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units.

The highest-priority comparisons are the high-aneuploidy PTEN boundaries and the residual CDKN2A contexts. PTEN loss has broad accepted support as a moderate stronger-dependency predictor, so H174 tests its high-aneuploidy main effect, H175 formally tests whether high aneuploidy modifies the PTEN contrast, and H187 tests the unresolved PTEN high-rnaseq_AXL boundary under relatively high Cas9 activity. H174 and H175 distinguish whether the broad PTEN signal survives a high genomic-instability background and whether any apparent context dependence is formal effect modification rather than a main high-aneuploidy subgroup effect.

For the accepted core markers, H179-H182 test high-aneuploidy main effects for SMARCA4 loss, TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, and MSI-high. These are robustness checks in a newly considered genomic background rather than new claims about aneuploidy-specific effect modification. H183 adds a formal SMARCA4 high-aneuploidy interaction because SMARCA4 loss is one of the strongest stronger-dependency predictors and an effect-modification test in this background is scientifically informative.

CDKN2A remains the main unresolved predictor. H176 tests whether any CDKN2A association remains after excluding deep 9p21 deletion, directly addressing possible confounding between CDKN2A loss and nearby 9p21 copy-number status. H186 tests a cleaner but likely narrow core-negative non-deep-9p21 background, excluding TP53, KEAP1, MSI-high, and SMARCA4 markers that can dominate the main marker map. H184 and H185 test reduced-marker high-EMT and high-hypoxia contexts to determine whether a threshold-level CDKN2A signal persists after excluding the two strongest positive-dependency markers. These CDKN2A tests are interpreted cautiously because prior CDKN2A context claims repeatedly failed independent validation.

H177 and high-stemness active comparisons are deferred because the 12-slot limit favors the high-aneuploidy and CDKN2A-boundary set. No independent validation request is available. All results requested here are discovery-stage associations in the supplied dataset; they do not establish causality, mechanism, biological interpretation of constructed assays, or external generalizability.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

Iteration 14/25, stage appraise, attempt 2.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

H174, PTEN loss in high-aneuploidy cells, has signed estimate +0.305 with 95% CI +0.119 to +0.492. The point estimate is well above threshold and excludes zero; although the lower bound is below threshold, this context effect is coherent with the broad, independently supported PTEN-loss pattern. I accept it as a dataset-level high-aneuploidy main effect, not as evidence that aneuploidy modifies PTEN. H175, the corresponding PTEN-by-high-aneuploidy interaction, is +0.086 with CI -0.129 to +0.301. The registered interaction is not established, but the interval still admits a meaningful positive interaction, so I keep it unresolved and close the investigation because the comparison has been performed. The high-aneuploidy robustness checks are all strong and entirely above threshold: SMARCA4 loss H179 +0.779, TP53 loss H180 +0.907, KEAP1 loss H181 +0.898, and MSI-high H182 +0.905. I accept each as a dataset-level context-robust association, not as proof of aneuploidy-specific effect modification. H183, the SMARCA4-by-high-aneuploidy interaction, is -0.032 with CI -0.191 to +0.126; even the upper bound is below the claimed threshold, so the registered interaction is rejected. CDKN2A remains fragile. H176, CDKN2A excluding deep 9p21 deletion, is +0.289 with CI +0.043 to +0.536, but only 27 exposed observations and a lower bound far below threshold; given repeated CDKN2A validation failures, I keep it unresolved. H184, CDKN2A in MSI/SMARCA4-negative high-EMT cells, is +0.300 with CI +0.128 to +0.472; it is the strongest new CDKN2A signal but still imprecise and contextually incomplete, so I keep it unresolved rather than accepting another near-threshold CDKN2A context. H185, CDKN2A in MSI/SMARCA4-negative high-hypoxia cells, is +0.145 with CI -0.009 to +0.299, below threshold and not excluding zero; I reject the registered context claim as unsupported, not as proof of no effect. H187, PTEN loss under high Cas9 activity and high AXL, is +0.159 with CI -0.037 to +0.355, too imprecise to establish this boundary context. H186 was invalid due to an exposed cell size below the required minimum, so it remains unresolved and closed. No validation was requested because no voluntary validation requests remain. All conclusions are dataset-level associations only and do not establish causality, mechanism, biological interpretation of constructed assays, or external generalizability.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect

record.narrative: Iteration 14 synthesis and final scientific report. Signed convention: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate means exposed minus comparator has stronger measured dependency (more negative dependency_composite); for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means weaker measured dependency. The effect-size threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units in the claimed direction. Due validation assessment: H158 tested CDKN2A loss in high aneuploidy cells with direction -1 (stronger dependency). Discovery estimate R149 is +0.283 (95% Welch interval +0.118 to +0.449), which is direction-consistent and near threshold, but the independent validation estimate R156 is only +0.048 with a conservative interval -0.184 to +0.280. The validation point estimate is below threshold and does not exclude zero, so the combined discovery-and-validation evidence does not support the registered claim. H158 is therefore rejected and closed. This is a failure to support CDKN2A in this context, not proof that CDKN2A has no effect in any context. Together with the validated-negative high-MYC context H127 and the validated-negative core-negative high-aneuploidy context H165, CDKN2A loss now has no robust dataset-level threshold support in this supplied dataset. Supported dataset-level findings. SMARCA4 loss is the strongest stronger-dependency association: main signed estimate +0.804 (95% interval +0.742 to +0.867) and independent validation +0.803 (+0.712 to +0.894). It remains strong in high-aneuploidy cells (+0.779, +0.636 to +0.922) and in several expression, marker, and copy-number-robust contexts; the formal SMARCA4-by-high-aneuploidy interaction H183 was rejected. MSI-high status is also strongly associated with stronger measured dependency: main signed estimate +0.775 (+0.664 to +0.885) and validation +0.831 (+0.668 to +0.993), with accepted subgroup and context checks but no established effect-modification contrasts. TP53 loss is strongly associated with weaker measured dependency (direction +1): main signed estimate +0.829 (+0.767 to +0.891) and validation +0.771 (+0.673 to +0.868). KEAP1 loss is also strongly associated with weaker measured dependency: main signed estimate +0.810 (+0.745 to +0.875) and validation +0.840 (+0.754 to +0.926). These core effects are robust across high-aneuploidy, MYC/AXL-expression, hypoxia, EMT, research-signature, marker-background, and library subsets. Formal interactions for these markers are mostly rejected or remain unresolved but are not needed for the main-effect conclusions. PTEN loss is a moderately and broadly supported stronger-dependency association: main discovery +0.239 (+0.145 to +0.332) and independent validation +0.294 (+0.149 to +0.439). Context-specific accepted support includes TP53-negative, KEAP1-negative, Avana-library, high-MYC, high-aneuploidy main-effect, high-Cas9, and lower-Cas9 settings. However, context dependence is not established: PTEN-by-high-aneuploidy interaction remains unresolved and closed, PTEN-by-high-AXL interaction was rejected, and several high-AXL or mutation-burden PTEN boundary estimates remain imprecise. Negative or unsupported comparisons include lineage subtype, KRAS mutation, EGFR amplification, BRAF V600E, MTAP loss, STK11 loss, MYC amplification, research markers D/E/F, sex, media-serum contrasts, screen batch, CRISPR-library and omics-availability contrasts, and most tested interactions. These are non-findings in this dataset under the stated threshold and uncertainty criteria. Unresolved uncertainty is concentrated in PTEN context boundaries and residual CDKN2A conditional signals. For PTEN, the broad signal is supported, but high-AXL and other subgroup estimates are near threshold with intervals spanning zero or lower bounds below threshold; the appropriate summary is a broad moderate association without confirmed context modification. For CDKN2A, multiple discovery-only contexts have positive point estimates around or above threshold, but the most plausible validated contexts failed. I closed the remaining active CDKN2A context H143 as a low-priority non-robust line; that is a prioritization decision, not an empirical rejection of that exact comparison. Most informative next analysis, if discovery-only work continues, is to run the already active robustness checks for the supported core effects: PTEN in high-stemness, high-EMT, and high-hypoxia contexts (H141, H145, H147), plus core-marker high-stemness checks H151-H153 and KEAP1 high-EMT H146. The active PTEN core-negative high-aneuploidy comparison H177 is scientifically informative but may be cell-count limited; if analyzed, interpret it as a cautiously qualified main-effect check, not an interaction test, and do not overstate it if below threshold or invalid. Further CDKN2A tests should generally wait unless a new, well-powered context with a credible validation path exists. Since no validation requests remain, any future results can refine discovery-level descriptions but cannot independently validate new claims in this run. All conclusions are dataset-level associations in the supplied 2000-line lung dataset. They do not establish causality, a single-gene knockout mechanism, biological meaning of constructed research assays, or external generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 15/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Iteration 15/25, stage explore, attempt 2.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.

prompt:
Iteration 15/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample.
