The validation point estimate is below threshold and does not exclude zero, so the combined discovery-and-validation evidence does not support the registered claim. H158 is therefore rejected and closed. This is a failure to support CDKN2A in this context, not proof that CDKN2A has no effect in any context. Together with the validated-negative high-MYC context H127 and the validated-negative core-negative high-aneuploidy context H165, CDKN2A loss now has no robust dataset-level threshold support in this supplied dataset. Supported dataset-level findings. SMARCA4 loss is the strongest stronger-dependency association: main signed estimate +0.804 (95% interval +0.742 to +0.867) and independent validation +0.803 (+0.712 to +0.894). It remains strong in high-aneuploidy cells (+0.779, +0.636 to +0.922) and in several expression, marker, and copy-number-robust contexts; the formal SMARCA4-by-high-aneuploidy interaction H183 was rejected. MSI-high status is also strongly associated with stronger measured dependency: main signed estimate +0.775 (+0.664 to +0.885) and validation +0.831 (+0.668 to +0.993), with accepted subgroup and context checks but no established effect-modification contrasts. TP53 loss is strongly associated with weaker measured dependency (direction +1): main signed estimate +0.829 (+0.767 to +0.891) and validation +0.771 (+0.673 to +0.868). KEAP1 loss is also strongly associated with weaker measured dependency: main signed estimate +0.810 (+0.745 to +0.875) and validation +0.840 (+0.754 to +0.926). These core effects are robust across high-aneuploidy, MYC/AXL-expression, hypoxia, EMT, research-signature, marker-background, and library subsets. Formal interactions for these markers are mostly rejected or remain unresolved but are not needed for the main-effect conclusions. PTEN loss is a moderately and broadly supported stronger-dependency association: main discovery +0.239 (+0.145 to +0.332) and independent validation +0.294 (+0.149 to +0.439). Context-specific accepted support includes TP53-negative, KEAP1-negative, Avana-library, high-MYC, high-aneuploidy main-effect, high-Cas9, and lower-Cas9 settings. However, context dependence is not established: PTEN-by-high-aneuploidy interaction remains unresolved and closed, PTEN-by-high-AXL interaction was rejected, and several high-AXL or mutation-burden PTEN boundary estimates remain imprecise. These are non-findings in this dataset under the stated threshold and uncertainty criteria. Unresolved uncertainty is concentrated in PTEN context boundaries and residual CDKN2A conditional signals. For PTEN, the broad signal is supported, but high-AXL and other subgroup estimates are near threshold with intervals spanning zero or lower bounds below threshold; the appropriate summary is a broad moderate association without confirmed context modification. For CDKN2A, multiple discovery-only contexts have positive point estimates around or above threshold, but the most plausible validated contexts failed. I closed the remaining active CDKN2A context H143 as a low-priority non-robust line; that is a prioritization decision, not an empirical rejection of that exact comparison. Most informative next analysis, if discovery-only work continues, is to run the already active robustness checks for the supported core effects: PTEN in high-stemness, high-EMT, and high-hypoxia contexts (H141, H145, H147), plus core-marker high-stemness checks H151-H153 and KEAP1 high-EMT H146. Further CDKN2A tests should generally wait unless a new, well-powered context with a credible validation path exists. Since no validation requests remain, any future results can refine discovery-level descriptions but cannot independently validate new claims in this run. All conclusions are dataset-level associations in the supplied 2000-line lung dataset. record.narrative: No assessments are due. I selected twelve existing untested claims to resolve PTEN context boundaries and high-stemness robustness for supported core markers. Signed convention: direction -1 positive signed estimate means stronger measured dependency; direction +1 positive signed estimate means weaker measured dependency; threshold 0.15 composite dependency-score units. H141/H145/H147 test PTEN loss in broad high-stemness, high-EMT, and high-hypoxia contexts; H189 formally tests the PTEN-by-high-stemness interaction. H177 and H188 test PTEN in core-marker-negative high-aneuploidy and high-stemness backgrounds; these are cautious main-effect boundary checks and may be imprecise. H146 tests KEAP1 loss in high EMT, direction +1. H151/H152/H153 test broad SMARCA4, TP53, and KEAP1 high-stemness main effects; H190/H192 test core-negative high-stemness refinements for SMARCA4 and KEAP1. I omitted H191 because its eligibility requires tp53_loss=0 while the exposure is tp53_loss, making the exposed cell logically empty; H191 is closed as a registration/design issue, not an empirical rejection. I registered a corrected TP53 high-stemness core-negative comparison for later analysis, linked to the accepted TP53 main effect. If any selected comparison fails the 20-per-cell requirement, it should remain unresolved or be closed without inference. All requested analyses are dataset-level discovery associations; they do not establish causality, mechanism, biological meaning of constructed assays, or generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 15/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: Assessing under the signed convention: direction -1 positive means stronger measured dependency in the exposed group; direction +1 positive means weaker measured dependency in the exposed group; threshold is 0.15 composite units. H141 (PTEN loss, high stemness) is +0.344 (95% CI +0.184 to +0.504), well above threshold and excluding zero; accept. H145 (PTEN loss, high EMT) is +0.321 (+0.013 to +0.628); the point estimate is meaningful and directionally consistent with the validated broad PTEN-loss association, but the exposed cell is only 25 and the lower interval is near zero. I accept it cautiously as a discovery-level context check, not as robust subgroup-specific evidence or as evidence of EMT modification. H147 (PTEN loss, high hypoxia) is +0.312 (+0.140 to +0.484); accept. H188 (PTEN loss in TP53/KEAP1/MSI/SMARCA4-negative high-stemness cells) is +0.231 (+0.088 to +0.374); the point exceeds threshold and excludes zero, so I accept it cautiously as a core-negative high-stemness robustness check despite imperfect precision. In contrast, H177 (PTEN loss in core-negative high-aneuploidy cells) is +0.143 (-0.003 to +0.289); the point is below threshold and the interval includes zero, so the registered association is unsupported and rejected, not refuted. The PTEN-by-high-stemness interaction H189 is +0.149 (-0.047 to +0.345); the point is just below threshold, zero is included, but the interval still admits a meaningful positive interaction. Keep this unresolved but close the formal interaction check. The high-stemness robustness checks for core markers are strong: H151 SMARCA4 loss +0.703 (+0.579 to +0.828), H152 TP53 loss +0.863 (+0.752 to +0.974), H153 KEAP1 loss +0.774 (+0.650 to +0.898). The core-negative high-stemness refinements are equally strong: H190 SMARCA4 loss +0.723 (+0.645 to +0.801) and H192 KEAP1 loss +0.801 (+0.716 to +0.885). All accept as dataset-level associations. H146 KEAP1 loss in high EMT is +0.781 (+0.604 to +0.957); accept. Multiplicity remains relevant: the accepted PTEN context checks are mostly robustness of an already validated broad PTEN main effect, not independent evidence of context modification. No validation request is made because none remain. These are supplied-dataset associations only, not causal, mechanistic, or generalizable findings.

prompt:
Iteration 15/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

record.narrative: At this synthesis stage I assessed the sole due validation deadline, H165, and also reassessed H57 because independent validation evidence is now present. Under the signed convention, for direction -1 a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency. The threshold is 0.15 composite units. H165 tested CDKN2A loss as a stronger-dependency association in TP53/KEAP1/MSI/SMARCA4-negative cells with high aneuploidy. Discovery R160 gave +0.271 with 95% Welch interval +0.146 to +0.397, a borderline positive signal because the lower bound is just below threshold. The independent validation R169 gave +0.085 with interval -0.055 to +0.225; the validation point is below threshold and the interval includes zero. The combined discovery and validation evidence therefore does not support the registered claim, so H165 remains rejected and closed. This is a failure to support CDKN2A in this context, not proof of absence. This reinforces the pattern from H158 and H127, where CDKN2A discovery signals did not survive independent validation, and leaves no robust dataset-level CDKN2A association above threshold in the supplied data. H57 tested SMARCA4 loss by high research_signature_a effect modification; discovery R51 +0.014 interval -0.151 to +0.180 and validation R105 +0.062 interval -0.218 to +0.342 are below threshold and compatible with null, so I reassess it as rejected and closed. Scientific report: SMARCA4 loss has the strongest supported stronger-dependency association, main R40 +0.804 interval +0.742 to +0.867 and validation R65 +0.803 interval +0.712 to +0.894, with robust context checks including high aneuploidy and expression/marker backgrounds; effect-modification interactions such as H183 and H57 are not supported. MSI-high is strongly associated with stronger dependency, main R10 +0.775 interval +0.664 to +0.885 and validation R92 +0.831 interval +0.668 to +0.993, with accepted subgroup checks but no established interaction. TP53 loss is strongly associated with weaker dependency, main R11 +0.829 interval +0.767 to +0.891 and validation R78 +0.771 interval +0.673 to +0.868, robust across aneuploidy, expression, hypoxia, EMT, stemness, marker and library subsets. KEAP1 loss is similarly associated with weaker dependency, main R7 signed +0.810 interval +0.745 to +0.875 and validation R52 +0.840 interval +0.754 to +0.926, robust across contexts. PTEN loss is a moderate, broadly supported stronger-dependency association, main R8 +0.239 interval +0.145 to +0.332 and validation R13 +0.294 interval +0.149 to +0.439, with accepted robustness checks in TP53-negative, KEAP1-negative, Avana, high MYC, high AXL, high Cas9, low Cas9, high stemness, high EMT, high hypoxia, and core-negative high-stemness backgrounds, but PTEN context modification remains not established because interactions and some narrow core-negative estimates are imprecise or rejected, including H177 and H175/H178/H189. Negative or unsupported comparisons include lineage subtype H1, KRAS H2, EGFR amplification H3, BRAF V600E H4, MTAP H5, STK11 H6, MYC amplification H9, research markers D/E/F H12/H20/H21, sex H94, media serum contrasts H106/H109, screen batch H107, CRISPR-library and omics-availability contrasts H92/H108/H121/H93/H110/H120, and most tested interactions. CDKN2A has many conditional discovery point estimates near or above threshold but failed independent validation in high MYC H127, high aneuploidy H158, and core-negative high aneuploidy H165, so it remains unresolved at the level of robust dataset-level evidence and is currently not accepted. Unresolved uncertainty is mainly PTEN context boundaries and a small number of discovery-only conditional CDKN2A or PTEN checks; these do not undermine the validated main effects. The most informative next discovery-only analysis is to run the missing TP53 core-negative high-stemness main-effect check, represented by H193, to complete the high-stemness robustness table for the accepted core markers; if continued, PTEN interactions should be interpreted cautiously and pre-specified, and further CDKN2A tests should generally wait unless a higher-powered validation path exists. Because no validation requests remain, any future analyses can only refine discovery-level descriptions, not independently validate new claims. All conclusions are dataset-level associations in the supplied 2000-line lung dataset and do not establish causality, single-gene mechanism, biological meaning of constructed assays, or generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 16/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No claims are due for assessment. I selected the twelve active untested claims H194-H205. These complete a focused robustness and boundary analysis for the accepted dataset-level associations. First, H194-H197 test whether PTEN loss, SMARCA4 loss, TP53 loss, and KEAP1 loss remain associated with dependency in higher-quality screens defined by screen_roc_auc >= 0.95. Second, H198-H201 test the same four markers in faster-growth cultures defined by growth_rate_doublings_per_day >= 0.6. Third, H202-H205 test PTEN-specific boundaries: low screen quality (screen_roc_auc <= 0.93), slow growth (growth_rate <= 0.348), core-marker-negative high hypoxia, and high Wnt activity. These comparisons are scientifically useful because accepted marker effects should not be limited to high-quality or fast-growing subsets unless they are technical or proliferation confounds, and PTEN is a moderate association where context boundaries are especially informative. Signed interpretation: for direction -1 claims (PTEN and SMARCA4), positive signed estimates mean stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 claims (TP53 and KEAP1), positive signed estimates mean weaker dependency in the exposed group. The meaningful-effect threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. I omitted H193 from this batch because the twelve selected comparisons directly address quality/growth robustness and PTEN-specific context boundaries, and H193 is currently marked closed in the ledger with no evidence; it can be reconsidered later if reopening is scientifically justified. All requested results are discovery-only associations in the supplied dataset, with cell-size validity and multiplicity to be assessed after results arrive. They do not establish causality, single-gene mechanism, biological meaning of constructed assays, or generalizability.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: Assessment uses the signed convention: direction -1 positive means stronger dependency in the exposed group; direction +1 positive means weaker dependency in the exposed group. The meaningful-effect threshold is 0.15 composite units. In high-quality screen subsets (screen_roc_auc >= 0.95), SMARCA4 loss (R195 +0.814, lower +0.733), TP53 loss (R196 +0.840, lower +0.760), and KEAP1 loss (R197 +0.789, lower +0.703) remain strong accepted dataset-level associations. PTEN loss in this subset is R194 +0.192, CI +0.069 to +0.315. The point exceeds threshold and excludes zero, and PTEN has already been validated broadly; I accept it cautiously as robustness of the accepted PTEN association, not as precise independent proof that high-quality screens alone exceed the threshold or as evidence of screen-quality modification. In faster-growth subsets (growth_rate >= 0.6), all four marker checks are clear: PTEN loss R198 +0.371, SMARCA4 loss R199 +0.784, TP53 loss R200 +0.922, KEAP1 loss R201 +0.765, with lower bounds above threshold; accept and close. For PTEN boundary checks, low screen quality R202 +0.364 and high Wnt activity R205 +0.367 are above threshold with lower bounds above threshold; accept as dataset-level context robustness, though high-Wnt is discovery-only and not independently validated. Slow growth R203 +0.145 with CI -0.055 to +0.345 is below threshold and compatible with null; reject as unsupported and close. H204, PTEN loss in core-negative high-hypoxia cells, gives R204 +0.283, CI +0.140 to +0.426, but the lower bound is just below threshold, the exposed cell is small, and H166 appears to be a closely comparable core-negative high-hypoxia check with a conflicting lower estimate (+0.162, lower +0.041). I therefore keep H204 unresolved/deferred rather than accepting it as a robust context-specific association. This does not undermine the validated main PTEN effect. Multiplicity remains relevant: many PTEN context checks are not independent evidence of effect modification. No context modification by screen quality, growth, hypoxia, or Wnt is established from these simple subgroup estimates; I registered two PTEN interaction checks to test context modification more directly. No independent validation can be requested because none remain. All conclusions are supplied-dataset associations, not causal, mechanistic, or generalizable claims.

prompt:
Iteration 16/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

I use the existing signed convention: more negative dependency_composite means stronger dependency; for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means exposed minus comparator was more negative, i.e. stronger dependency in the exposed group, while for direction +1 claims it means weaker dependency in the exposed group. The meaningful-effect threshold remains 0.15 composite dependency-score units. The accepted main associations—SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high as stronger dependency, TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss as weaker dependency, and PTEN loss as a moderate stronger dependency—have been robust in many contexts, including high screen quality and fast growth, but lower-screen-quality and slower-growth boundaries are less complete. I therefore registered main effects for SMARCA4, TP53, KEAP1, and MSI-high in lower-quality screen subsets, defined by screen_roc_auc <= 0.93, and in slower-growth subsets, defined by growth_rate_doublings_per_day <= 0.348. These are falsifiable robustness tests: if a marker association remains above threshold, it is less likely to be confined to high-quality or rapidly proliferating cultures; if the interval includes null or the point is below threshold, the subgroup boundary remains unresolved. I also registered direct PTEN-loss interactions with lower screen quality and with fast growth. These complement the already active direct PTEN-loss interactions with high hypoxia and high Wnt activity, H206 and H207, and test effect modification more directly than simple subgroup estimates. For these PTEN interaction claims, direction -1 means that positive signed evidence corresponds to a larger PTEN-loss stronger-dependency effect in the named subgroup than in the complement. Simple subgroup estimates suggest stronger PTEN effects in low screen quality and fast growth, but those subgroup contrasts are imprecise and do not establish modification; the new interaction contrasts are the better test. If any comparison has insufficient cell count, that is a design limitation rather than empirical rejection. All conclusions remain supplied-dataset associations, not causal claims, mechanistic claims, or claims of generalizability.

prompt:
Iteration 17/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative:
Interpretation follows the signed convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed or subgroup condition; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed or subgroup condition. The meaningful-effect threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units.

The simple subgroup robustness comparisons are strong. In lower-screen-quality subsets (screen_roc_auc <= 0.93), SMARCA4 loss shows +0.768 [0.642, 0.895], TP53 loss +0.840 [0.708, 0.971], KEAP1 loss +0.854 [0.719, 0.989], and MSI-high +0.839 [0.559, 1.118]. In slower-growth subsets (growth_rate_doublings_per_day <= 0.348), SMARCA4 loss shows +0.875 [0.745, 1.004], TP53 loss +0.846 [0.709, 0.983], KEAP1 loss +0.844 [0.706, 0.982], and MSI-high +0.498 [0.220, 0.776]. All point estimates and lower bounds exceed the threshold and exclude zero, so I accept H208-H215 as dataset-level evidence that the main marker associations persist in these technical and proliferation contexts. The MSI checks use exposed cells of 28 and 25, respectively, so they meet the minimum-cell rule but are less precise; their lower bounds are still above threshold. These subgroup results should not be read as effect-modification results because they are not interaction contrasts.

The direct PTEN-loss interaction contrasts are much less supportive of effect modification. H206 high hypoxia gives +0.102 [-0.102, 0.306], which is below threshold and includes the null. H207 high Wnt gives +0.184 [-0.011, 0.379], H216 lower screen quality gives +0.173 [-0.031, 0.376], and H217 faster growth gives +0.171 [-0.053, 0.396]. The latter three point estimates exceed 0.15, but their intervals include negative values and therefore include no interaction; the uncertainty is too wide to accept a meaningful PTEN interaction. I record these as unresolved/closed rather than accepted, because the evidence does not support modification, while the intervals are not sufficiently narrow to justify a definitive rejection of a modest positive modification. Overall, the data do not establish PTEN effect modification by hypoxia, Wnt activity, screen quality, or growth rate.

Multiplicity remains a concern: many context-specific comparisons have been run, and some intervals include meaningful positive effects merely because of imprecision. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so these are discovery associations in the supplied dataset only. They do not establish causality, single-gene mechanism, pathway meaning, or generalizability beyond this dataset.

Iteration 17/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due and no independent validation requests remain. I therefore leave the controller-maintained accepted set unchanged. The controller reports no remaining new validation capacity and no listed response deadline. The synthesis below uses the ledger signed estimates and the 0.15 composite-unit absolute threshold.

Signed convention. More negative dependency_composite means stronger dependency. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means exposed minus comparator was more negative, i.e. stronger dependency in the exposed condition. For direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means exposed minus comparator was less negative, i.e. weaker dependency in the exposed condition.

Supported main effects in the supplied dataset. SMARCA4 loss is a strong stronger-dependency association. H43/R40 gives +0.804 [0.742, 0.867] and validation R65 gives +0.803 [0.712, 0.894]. H43 is also accepted in many context-specific mean comparisons, including lower-screen-quality and slower-growth subsets H208/R208 and H212/R212.

MSI-high is a strong stronger-dependency association. H10/R10 gives +0.775 [0.664, 0.885] and validation R92 gives +0.831 [0.668, 0.993]. Subgroup mean checks are generally robust, including lower-screen-quality H211/R211 and slower-growth H215/R215, though MSI-high exposed cells are smaller in those checks.

TP53 loss is a strong weaker-dependency association. H11/R11 gives +0.829 [0.767, 0.891] and validation R78 gives +0.771 [0.673, 0.868]. It is robust across many clinical, technical, omics, lineage, signature, mutation-burden, screen-quality, growth-rate, and pathway-score contexts.

KEAP1 loss is a strong weaker-dependency association. H13/R7 gives +0.810 [0.745, 0.875] and validation R52 gives +0.840 [0.754, 0.926]. It is robust across many contexts, including lower-screen-quality H210/R210 and slower-growth H214/R214.

PTEN loss is a moderate stronger-dependency association. H8/R8 gives +0.239 [0.145, 0.332] and validation R13 gives +0.294 [0.149, 0.439]. It is also supported in many contexts, including TP53-negative H22/R17, KEAP1-negative H28/R22 and R39, Avana H35/R25, PIK3CA-positive H45/R41, high MYC H116/R121 and R130, high AXL, high Cas9, stemness, EMT, hypoxia, aneuploidy, high and low screen quality, and fast growth. The H116 validation is directionally positive but imprecise, with lower bound near zero, so it supports the main PTEN effect more than the high-MYC modification itself.

Context robustness is not the same as effect modification. The direct interaction contrasts that have been tested for the major markers are mostly null or imprecise. SMARCA4 interactions with subtype H44/R94, signature A H57/R51 and R105, and aneuploidy H183/R176 do not support modification. MSI-high subtype interaction H86/R80 is rejected. KEAP1 interaction with SMARCA4 loss H88/R82 is rejected. PTEN interactions with KEAP1-negative H89/R83, hypoxia H206/R206, high Wnt H207/R207, lower screen quality H216/R216, and fast growth H217/R217 do not support accepted modification. The latter three PTEN interaction points exceed 0.15, but their intervals include zero and values below threshold; H206 is below threshold. Therefore PTEN effect modification remains unresolved in the sense of not established, but not demonstrable with these contrasts.

Negative or unsupported comparisons include many broad main-effect nulls: lineage subtype H1/R1, KRAS H2/R2, EGFR amplification H3/R3, BRAF V600E H4/R4 and validation R79, MTAP H5/R5, STK11 H6/R6, MYC amplification H9/R9, research markers D/E/F H20/R35, H12/R12, and H21/R36, sex H94/R98, media H106/R111 and H109/R114, batch H107/R112, CRISPR-library and omics availability H92/R96, H108/R113, H121/R126, H93/R97, H110/R115, and H120/R125. Secondary markers tested in core-negative contexts are generally unsupported or near threshold, including ERBB2, PIK3CA, SMAD4, APC, NF1, BRCA2, RB1, and ARID1A.

CDKN2A loss is not robustly supported. Some core-negative discovery estimates are near or above 0.15, such as R95 and R48, but independent validation failed in high MYC H127/R143, high aneuploidy H158/R156, and core-negative high aneuploidy H165/R169. Direct CDKN2A interactions tested were also not accepted. Thus CDKN2A is treated as not meaningfully associated after multiplicity and validation failure, while invalid underpowered checks are treated as design limitations rather than empirical rejections.

Unresolved uncertainty. The main unresolved scientific issue is whether PTEN has context-specific effect modification, especially by hypoxia and possibly Wnt, screen quality, or growth rate. Existing all-population interaction estimates are imprecise. Some core-negative PTEN subgroup means are near threshold but not decisive, such as high hypoxia R204 and high AXL R165/R168. Several deferred contrasts remain untested, including PTEN in PIK3CA-negative H23 and PTEN in non-Avana H64. These do not undermine the validated main effects above.

Most informative next analyses. Because validation capacity is exhausted, I registered discovery direct interactions rather than further validations: direct marker interactions for SMARCA4, TP53, KEAP1, and MSI-high in lower-quality screen subsets and slower-growth subsets, plus core-negative PTEN interactions with high hypoxia and high stemness. These tests ask whether the context changes the marker effect rather than merely whether the marker effect remains visible in the context. Future acceptance should require the direct interaction interval to support the claimed direction and the effect-size threshold; otherwise accepted subgroup mean differences should be reported as robustness only. All conclusions remain associations in the supplied 2000-line lung dataset and do not establish causality, single-gene mechanism, biological meaning of constructed signatures or markers, or generalizability beyond this dataset.

Iteration 18/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.
