SMARCA4 interactions with subtype H44/R94, signature A H57/R51 and R105, and aneuploidy H183/R176 do not support modification. MSI-high subtype interaction H86/R80 is rejected. KEAP1 interaction with SMARCA4 loss H88/R82 is rejected. PTEN interactions with KEAP1-negative H89/R83, hypoxia H206/R206, high Wnt H207/R207, lower screen quality H216/R216, and fast growth H217/R217 do not support accepted modification. The latter three PTEN interaction points exceed 0.15, but their intervals include zero and values below threshold; H206 is below threshold. Therefore PTEN effect modification remains unresolved in the sense of not established, but not demonstrable with these contrasts.\n\nNegative or unsupported comparisons include many broad main-effect nulls: lineage subtype H1/R1, KRAS H2/R2, EGFR amplification H3/R3, BRAF V600E H4/R4 and validation R79, MTAP H5/R5, STK11 H6/R6, MYC amplification H9/R9, research markers D/E/F H20/R35, H12/R12, and H21/R36, sex H94/R98, media H106/R111 and H109/R114, batch H107/R112, CRISPR-library and omics availability H92/R96, H108/R113, H121/R126, H93/R97, H110/R115, and H120/R125. Secondary markers tested in core-negative contexts are generally unsupported or near threshold, including ERBB2, PIK3CA, SMAD4, APC, NF1, BRCA2, RB1, and ARID1A.\n\nCDKN2A loss is not robustly supported. Some core-negative discovery estimates are near or above 0.15, such as R95 and R48, but independent validation failed in high MYC H127/R143, high aneuploidy H158/R156, and core-negative high aneuploidy H165/R169. Direct CDKN2A interactions tested were also not accepted. Thus CDKN2A is treated as not meaningfully associated after multiplicity and validation failure, while invalid underpowered checks are treated as design limitations rather than empirical rejections.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty. The main unresolved scientific issue is whether PTEN has context-specific effect modification, especially by hypoxia and possibly Wnt, screen quality, or growth rate. Existing all-population interaction estimates are imprecise. Some core-negative PTEN subgroup means are near threshold but not decisive, such as high hypoxia R204 and high AXL R165/R168. Several deferred contrasts remain untested, including PTEN in PIK3CA-negative H23 and PTEN in non-Avana H64. record.narrative: No assessments are due, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so these are discovery-only comparisons in the supplied dataset. The signed convention remains: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed or subgroup context; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means weaker dependency in the exposed or subgroup context. The meaningful-effect threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. The accepted main associations are SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high as stronger dependency, TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss as weaker dependency, and PTEN loss as a moderate stronger dependency. The main remaining PTEN uncertainty is whether its association is modified by biological or technical context. Existing simple subgroup estimates for PTEN suggest larger effects in lower screen quality and high MYC contexts, but simple subgroup means do not establish effect modification. I therefore register two direct PTEN-loss interaction refinements in the core-negative population (TP53 loss absent, KEAP1 loss absent, MSI-high absent, and SMARCA4 loss absent) to reduce confounding by the stronger main-effect markers. For the first proposal, the hypothesized modification is that PTEN loss has a stronger stronger-dependency association when screen_roc_auc <= 0.93 than in the complement of that subgroup within the same core-negative eligible population. The raw interaction contrast would then be negative because PTEN loss makes dependency more negative in the lower-quality subset than in the higher-quality complement; with direction -1, evidence for the hypothesis is a positive signed interaction estimate. The plausible alternative is no meaningful modification, or that any apparent subgroup elevation is technical noise or imprecision. For the second proposal, the hypothesized modification is that PTEN loss has a stronger stronger-dependency association when rnaseq_MYC_log2_tpm >= 5.5 than in the complement within the same core-negative population. This raw interaction would also be negative if PTEN loss makes dependency more negative in high-MYC contexts; direction -1 again maps this to a positive signed estimate. The plausible alternative is that PTEN loss remains context-independent, with any apparent MYC-context elevation arising from confounding by lineage, proliferation, or multiplicity. I rank these new direct PTEN interactions alongside the active marker robustness interactions and core-negative PTEN interactions with hypoxia and stemness. If analysis capacity is constrained, prioritize the active direct marker interactions, then core-negative PTEN interactions. Insufficient cell counts would be treated as design limitations rather than empirical nulls. All conclusions remain dataset-level associations, not causal, mechanistic, or generalizable claims.

Iteration 18/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

prompt:
Iteration 18/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve new comparisons are direct interaction contrasts, not simple subgroup mean differences, and all passed the minimum-cell rule. Under the signed convention, direction -1 expects a positive signed interaction for stronger dependency in the named context relative to its complement, and direction +1 expects a positive signed interaction for a larger weaker-dependency effect in the named context. The absolute threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. None of these twelve new results supports the registered effect-modification hypotheses. H218 rejects claimed SMARCA4-loss modification by lower screen quality because the signed estimate is -0.048 with upper bound 0.097, below the meaningful positive threshold; the data exclude the claimed positive modification, though they do not precisely exclude small opposite changes. H227 rejects claimed PTEN-loss modification by high stemness because the signed estimate is -0.040 with upper bound 0.130, below the positive threshold. H225 and H229 also reject the registered directions. H225 has a signed MSI-high interaction of -0.368 with interval [-0.672, -0.064], and H229 has a signed PTEN high-MYC interaction of -0.187 with interval [-0.343, -0.031]. Both intervals exclude the claimed positive direction and instead point to attenuation of the marker association in those contexts. If reversed, their absolute magnitude intervals are 0.064 to 0.672 and 0.031 to 0.343 respectively; the point estimates exceed 0.15, but the lower bounds do not, so they are possible attenuation signals rather than accepted meaningful reversed effects. The remaining unresolved claims, H219-H224, H226, and H228, have point estimates mostly below 0.15 and intervals that include zero and values above threshold, so they are inconclusive rather than evidence of modification. H221, H222, and H224 have relatively small or wide uncertainty despite valid cell counts. Multiplicity is a serious concern because many technical, proliferation, expression, and pathway contexts have now been examined. Therefore, the supplied dataset does not establish accepted effect modification of SMARCA4 loss, TP53 loss, KEAP1 loss, MSI-high, or PTEN loss by lower screen quality, slower growth, high hypoxia, high stemness, or high MYC in the core-negative population. The accepted main dataset associations remain unchanged: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are strong stronger-dependency markers, TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are strong weaker-dependency markers, and PTEN loss is a moderate stronger-dependency marker. Simple subgroup mean differences in those contexts are robustness evidence only, not causal or generalized effect modification.

Iteration 18/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units

record.narrative:
No response deadlines are listed and no assessment requests are due, and the controller reports no remaining new independent validation requests. I therefore assessed all validation estimates currently present in the ledger as evidence already reflected in the maintained claim set: H4/R79 supports rejection of a meaningful BRAF V600E weaker-dependency association; H7/H13/R52 supports robust KEAP1-loss weaker-dependency; H8/R13 supports PTEN-loss stronger-dependency; H10/R92 supports MSI-high stronger-dependency; H11/R78 supports TP53-loss weaker-dependency; H28/R39 supports PTEN loss in KEAP1-negative cells; H40/R38 and H43/R65 support SMARCA4-loss stronger-dependency; H57/R105 does not support SMARCA4-loss modification by high signature A; H116/R130 supports the main PTEN-loss association in high-MYC cells but is imprecise; H127/R143, H158/R156, and H165/R169 are independent evidence against robust CDKN2A-loss association in high-MYC and aneuploid contexts. The accepted controller-maintained set is unchanged.

Main supported findings in the supplied 2000-line dataset. The outcome threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. More negative dependency_composite means stronger dependency. Under the signed convention, direction -1 claims are positive when the exposed condition shows stronger dependency, and direction +1 claims are positive when the exposed condition shows weaker dependency. SMARCA4 loss is a strong stronger-dependency association: discovery H43/R40 is +0.804 [0.742, 0.867] and validation R65 is +0.803 [0.712, 0.894]. MSI-high is a strong stronger-dependency association: H10/R10 is +0.775 [0.664, 0.885] and validation R92 is +0.831 [0.668, 0.993]. TP53 loss is a strong weaker-dependency association: H11/R11 is +0.829 [0.767, 0.891] and validation R78 is +0.771 [0.673, 0.868]. KEAP1 loss is a strong weaker-dependency association: H13/R7 is +0.810 [0.745, 0.875] and validation R52 is +0.840 [0.754, 0.926]. PTEN loss is a moderate stronger-dependency association: H8/R8 is +0.239 [0.145, 0.332] and validation R13 is +0.294 [0.149, 0.439]. These are dataset-level associations, not causal or mechanistic claims, and the endpoint is composite rather than a single-gene knockout measurement.

Context-specific subgroup means remain robustness evidence, not established effect modification. The four strongest marker associations and the PTEN association appear visible in many clinical, technical, omics, lineage, screen-quality, growth-rate, mutation-burden, and pathway-score contexts. However, direct interaction tests generally do not establish that the effect changes across those contexts. SMARCA4-loss modifications by subtype, signature A, lower screen quality, and aneuploidy are not supported; MSI-high subtype interaction is rejected; KEAP1 interaction with SMARCA4 loss is rejected. PTEN interactions with lineage, PIK3CA status, KEAP1-negative status, AXL all-population, lower screen quality, fast growth, hypoxia, stemness, and core-negative hypoxia, stemness, or screen quality do not provide accepted evidence of modification. The most notable direct interaction signals remain imprecise rather than conclusive: all-population PTEN high-Wnt interaction R207 is +0.184 [-0.011, 0.379]; all-population PTEN lower-screen-quality interaction R216 is +0.173 [-0.031, 0.376]; all-population PTEN fast-growth interaction R217 is +0.171 [-0.053, 0.396]. These are compatible with possible PTEN modification but do not support acceptance under the stated interaction standard.

Two reversed attenuation signals should be interpreted cautiously. H229 registered a stronger PTEN effect in core-negative high-MYC cells versus complement and was rejected for that direction; its signed estimate is -0.187 [-0.343, -0.031], which favors attenuation of the PTEN association in high-MYC core-negative cells. The reversed interval is +0.187 [0.031, 0.343], with point above threshold but lower bound below threshold, so it is suggestive but not accepted. Similarly, H225 rejected a stronger MSI-high effect in slower-growing cells, while favoring attenuation; the reversed interval is +0.368 [0.064, 0.672], again with lower bound below threshold. These are possible attenuation patterns, not established effect modification.

Negative findings are broad. Many predictors show no meaningful association at the 0.15 threshold: lineage subtype, KRAS mutation, EGFR amplification, BRAF V600E, MTAP loss, STK11 loss, MYC amplification, research marker D, E, and F, sex, CRISPR-library indicators, omics availability, screen batch, media serum concentration contrasts, and several secondary core-negative markers. In particular, the constructed research markers and signatures do not behave as main dependency predictors, and their high-subgroup marker associations mostly reflect the robust main marker effects rather than evidence of constructed-assay modification.

CDKN2A loss is not robustly supported. Several core-negative discovery contrasts are near or above threshold, including R30, R48, and R95, but independent validation failed in high-MYC cells R143, high-aneuploidy cells R156, and core-negative high-aneuploidy cells R169. Direct CDKN2A interactions tested so far also do not establish modification. Invalid underpowered contrasts are design limitations, but they are not evidence of association. Therefore the best current conclusion is that CDKN2A loss is not a robustly associated dependency predictor in this dataset after validation and multiplicity.

Unresolved uncertainty. The main unresolved scientific issue is PTEN-loss effect modification. Existing robust subgroup means show PTEN associations in many contexts, but direct interactions are mostly null or imprecise. The high-Wnt, high-AXL, fast-growth, lower-screen-quality, high-MYC, and slower-growth interactions remain useful follow-up targets. The MSI-high slower-growth attenuation signal is a secondary unresolved question. The four registered proposals are focused discovery interactions rather than new validations because validation capacity is exhausted: direct PTEN-loss interaction with high Wnt and high AXL within the core-negative population; a formally reversed PTEN-loss high-MYC attenuation proposal; and a formally reversed MSI-high slower-growth attenuation proposal. For PTEN proposals, the hypothesis is that the PTEN-loss association is stronger in the named context than in the complementary core-negative cells; direction -1 makes a positive signed interaction evidence for that stronger context effect. For reversed attenuation proposals, direction +1 makes a positive signed interaction evidence that the marker association is weaker in the named context. Future acceptance should require the interaction interval to support the claimed direction and be compatible with the 0.15 threshold; otherwise robust subgroup means should be reported as robustness only. Insufficient cell counts, if encountered, should be treated as design limitations rather than empirical nulls.

Final scientific status. The supplied dataset supports SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high as strong stronger-dependency markers, TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss as strong weaker-dependency markers, and PTEN loss as a moderate stronger-dependency marker. It does not support broad technical, demographic, or most secondary molecular predictors. It does not establish meaningful effect modification of the major marker effects by the contexts tested so far, although PTEN contexts and two attenuation patterns remain possible but unresolved. CDKN2A is not robust. All conclusions are dataset-specific associations and do not establish causality, single-gene knockout mechanism, biological pathway interpretation, or generalizability beyond this dataset.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so all newly registered comparisons are discovery-only analyses in the supplied dataset. The outcome threshold remains 0.15 composite dependency-score units. More negative dependency_composite means stronger dependency. Under the signed convention, direction -1 claims are positive when the exposed condition or named subgroup shows a stronger-dependency effect, while direction +1 claims are positive when they show a weaker-dependency effect. The controller-maintained accepted main associations are SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high as strong stronger-dependency markers, TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss as strong weaker-dependency markers, and PTEN loss as a moderate stronger-dependency marker. No direct interaction has yet been accepted as meaningful effect modification. These new proposals are therefore refinements aimed at the remaining unresolved question: whether the accepted marker associations, especially PTEN loss, are genuinely modified by biological, proliferation, expression, or technical context, or whether context-specific subgroup means merely show robustness. For interaction tests, I will accept only if the signed interval supports the claimed direction and is compatible with the 0.15 threshold; point estimates above threshold with intervals including zero or values below threshold remain unresolved. Simple subgroup mean differences are not sufficient to establish modification. The first two proposals test whether high MYC expression modifies TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss, two accepted weaker-dependency markers. Both have simple subgroup means in high MYC that appear numerically larger than their overall marker means, so a direct interaction with rnaseq_MYC_log2_tpm at least 5.5 can determine whether this is true modification or confounding by population composition, lineage, proliferation, or screening context. The expected direction is positive for direction +1 claims if TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss show a larger weaker-dependency effect in high-MYC cells than in the complement. The plausible alternative is that high MYC does not modify these large marker effects and any apparent elevation is not reproducible as an interaction. The next two proposals address previously suggestive attenuation signals whose reversed intervals had lower bounds below threshold. For PTEN loss, H229 or H232 suggested attenuation of the PTEN stronger-dependency association in core-negative high-MYC cells using MYC at least 5.5. I register a broader attenuation test using rnaseq_MYC_log2_tpm at least 5.0 within the core-negative population to increase precision and test whether attenuation is a broader expression-threshold phenomenon rather than a highly selective subgroup artifact. Direction +1 makes a positive signed interaction evidence that the PTEN association is weaker in high-MYC cells than in the complement. For MSI-high, H225 or H233 suggested attenuation of the MSI-high stronger-dependency association in slower-growing cells defined by growth_rate_doublings_per_day at most 0.348. I register a broader median-based attenuation test using growth_rate_doublings_per_day at most 0.462, again direction +1, to test whether this attenuation persists when the named context is enlarged. The plausible alternative in both cases is that the attenuation signal was imprecise, threshold-specific, or confounded by other accepted markers, and no meaningful modification exists. The remaining proposals address PTEN-loss modification by technical screen quality and pathway or expression context. H216 gave a suggestive positive signed PTEN lower-screen-quality interaction using screen_roc_auc at most 0.93, but the interval crossed zero. I register a broader lower-quality test using screen_roc_auc at most 0.95. Direction -1 means a positive signed interaction would indicate that PTEN loss has a stronger-dependency association in lower-quality screen cells than in the higher-quality complement. The plausible alternative is that PTEN loss is not modified by screen quality and any apparent elevation reflects imprecision or confounding. For the core-negative PTEN interactions, the earlier high-Wnt all-population interaction R207 was suggestive but imprecise, and the core-negative high-AXL simple context estimate R165 was suggestive. I register two lower-threshold core-negative interaction tests: Wnt activity at least 0.25 and AXL expression at least 3.5, both direction -1. These increase sample size while still testing whether the PTEN association is context-specific within a population where the four strongest markers are absent, reducing confounding by the dominant marker effects. If these interactions are imprecise or null, PTEN context-specific subgroup means should continue to be reported only as robustness evidence, not as accepted effect modification. Insufficient cell counts would be treated as design limitations, not as empirical nulls. Multiplicity remains substantial, so any acceptance should require both size and interval support, not a nominally favorable point estimate. All conclusions remain dataset-level associations and do not establish causality, single-gene mechanism, biological meaning of constructed signatures or markers, or generalizability beyond this dataset.

prompt:
Iteration 19/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: No assessments are due, and independent validation capacity is exhausted, so I request only discovery analyses on existing registered claims. I select twelve untested claims to add new evidence. Nine are the newly registered active direct interactions H230, H231, H234, H235, H236, H237, H238, H239, and H240. They test whether accepted marker associations are genuinely context-modified: PTEN-loss modification by high Wnt or high AXL in core-negative cells, broader PTEN attenuation by MYC, PTEN modification by lower screen quality, TP53-loss and KEAP1-loss modification by high MYC, and broader MSI-high attenuation by slower growth. I do not select H232 or H233 in run_analyses because their displayed evidence already comes from R229 and R225; rerunning them would reuse existing data and not add a new sample, although they remain active for later assessment. I also request H132 and H133 because they are high-value untested direct interactions for SMARCA4 loss by high MYC and KEAP1 loss by high AXL, respectively. Finally, I request H23 as a well-powered subgroup robustness test of PTEN loss in PIK3CA-negative cells. All returned estimates and intervals are already signed to the claim direction. For direction -1, a positive signed effect corresponds to stronger dependency in the exposed condition or stronger-dependency effect in the named interaction context relative to its complement; for direction +1, a positive signed effect corresponds to weaker dependency or attenuation of the named marker association. The outcome threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. For interactions, I will accept only if the signed interval supports the claimed direction and is compatible with a meaningful effect above 0.15; point estimates above 0.15 with lower bounds below 0.15 will remain unresolved rather than accepted. Simple subgroup means such as H23 can support an accepted within-subgroup association if they meet size, direction, and interval criteria, but do not establish effect modification. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations and do not establish causality, single-gene mechanism, biological meaning of constructed assays, or generalizability beyond this dataset.

record.narrative: Under the signed convention, positive estimates support the registered direction, and the absolute threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. Direct interaction claims are accepted only when the signed interval supports the claimed direction and is also compatible with a meaningful magnitude above the threshold. With 95 percent Welch intervals, many of these interaction contrasts are still imprecise even though all valid cells met the minimum sample rule, and the run has examined many technical, expression, proliferation, and pathway contexts, so multiplicity requires caution. For direction -1 interactions, a positive signed value would indicate stronger dependency in the named context relative to its complement; for direction +1 interactions, a positive signed value would indicate a larger weaker-dependency effect, or attenuation, in the named context. Several new interactions are unresolved rather than supportive. H230, H235, H237, H238, H239, H240, and H133 have point estimates mostly below threshold, or point estimates near zero, and intervals that include zero, values below threshold, and values above threshold. They are therefore inconclusive as effect modification and do not justify acceptance. H234 and H236 are the most notable new results because their point estimates are above threshold: TP53-loss high-MYC interaction is +0.164 with lower bound +0.034, and PTEN-loss core-negative MYC at least 5.0 attenuation interaction is +0.173 with lower bound +0.019. Both support their registered directions, but their lower bounds fall well below 0.15. Under the stricter interaction standard, these are possible attenuation or context-strengthening signals but not accepted meaningful effect modification, especially because threshold choices and prior exploratory subgroup analyses increase selective reporting risk. H231 and H132 are rejections of the claimed stronger-context direction. H231 has signed estimate -0.097 with upper bound +0.089, so a meaningful positive stronger-PTEN effect in high-AXL core-negative cells is excluded by the interval even though small opposite effects remain possible. H132 has signed estimate -0.044 with upper bound +0.102, similarly excluding a meaningful stronger-SMARCA4-loss effect in high-MYC cells. These rejections are limited to the claimed direction and do not establish precise nullity for small opposite changes. H23 is a simple mean_difference within PIK3CA-negative cells, not an interaction. The PTEN-loss versus non-PTEN contrast in PIK3CA-negative cells is +0.211 with a 95 percent interval excluding zero and a point above threshold. It supports a dataset-level stronger-dependency association for PTEN loss in PIK3CA-negative cells and extends the accepted overall PTEN-loss robustness evidence. It should not be interpreted as effect modification because H32 did not support a PIK3CA-specific interaction. The main controller-maintained dataset associations remain unchanged: SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high are strong stronger-dependency markers, TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss are strong weaker-dependency markers, and PTEN loss is a moderate stronger-dependency marker. No new direct interaction has been accepted. Validation capacity is exhausted, so these conclusions remain dataset-specific associations without independent confirmation for the unresolved attenuation signals. Biological causality, single-gene mechanism, pathway interpretation, constructed-assay meaning, and generalizability beyond this dataset remain uncertain.

prompt:
Iteration 19/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_composite (composite dependency-score units). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use
previous results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are
both useful throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent
validation when useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

The endpoint is a composite dependency score; it does not represent a single gene's knockout measurement.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
Scientifically meaningful effects exceed the stated outcome-specific effect-size threshold in the claimed direction. Thresholds are absolute differences on the supplied outcome scale, not percentages of the outcome mean. Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of these thresholds. Acceptance does not require independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Outcome-specific absolute effect-size thresholds:
- dependency_composite: 0.15 composite dependency-score units
Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

The accepted controller-maintained set is unchanged.\n\nMain supported findings in the supplied 2000-line dataset. The outcome threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units. More negative dependency_composite means stronger dependency. Under the signed convention, direction -1 claims are positive when the exposed condition shows stronger dependency, and direction +1 claims are positive when the exposed condition shows weaker dependency. SMARCA4 loss is a strong stronger-dependency association: discovery H43/R40 is +0.804 [0.742, 0.867] and validation R65 is +0.803 [0.712, 0.894]. MSI-high is a strong stronger-dependency association: H10/R10 is +0.775 [0.664, 0.885] and validation R92 is +0.831 [0.668, 0.993]. TP53 loss is a strong weaker-dependency association: H11/R11 is +0.829 [0.767, 0.891] and validation R78 is +0.771 [0.673, 0.868]. KEAP1 loss is a strong weaker-dependency association: H13/R7 is +0.810 [0.745, 0.875] and validation R52 is +0.840 [0.754, 0.926]. PTEN loss is a moderate stronger-dependency association: H8/R8 is +0.239 [0.145, 0.332] and validation R13 is +0.294 [0.149, 0.439]. These are dataset-level associations, not causal or mechanistic claims, and the endpoint is composite rather than a single-gene knockout measurement.\n\nContext-specific subgroup means remain robustness evidence, not established effect modification. The four strongest marker associations and the PTEN association appear visible in many clinical, technical, omics, lineage, screen-quality, growth-rate, mutation-burden, and pathway-score contexts. However, direct interaction tests generally do not establish that the effect changes across those contexts. SMARCA4-loss modifications by subtype, signature A, lower screen quality, and aneuploidy are not supported; MSI-high subtype interaction is rejected; KEAP1 interaction with SMARCA4 loss is rejected. PTEN interactions with lineage, PIK3CA status, KEAP1-negative status, AXL all-population, lower screen quality, fast growth, hypoxia, stemness, and core-negative hypoxia, stemness, or screen quality do not provide accepted evidence of modification. The most notable direct interaction signals remain imprecise rather than conclusive: all-population PTEN high-Wnt interaction R207 is +0.184 [-0.011, 0.379]; all-population PTEN lower-screen-quality interaction R216 is +0.173 [-0.031, 0.376]; all-population PTEN fast-growth interaction R217 is +0.171 [-0.053, 0.396]. These are compatible with possible PTEN modification but do not support acceptance under the stated interaction standard.\n\nTwo reversed attenuation signals should be interpreted cautiously. H229 registered a stronger PTEN effect in core-negative high-MYC cells versus complement and was rejected for that direction; its signed estimate is -0.187 [-0.343, -0.031], which favors attenuation of the PTEN association in high-MYC core-negative cells. The reversed interval is +0.187 [0.031, 0.343], with point above threshold but lower bound below threshold, so it is suggestive but not accepted. Similarly, H225 rejected a stronger MSI-high effect in slower-growing cells, while favoring attenuation; the reversed interval is +0.368 [0.064, 0.672], again with lower bound below threshold. These are possible attenuation patterns, not established effect modification.\n\nNegative findings are broad. Many predictors show no meaningful association at the 0.15 threshold: lineage subtype, KRAS mutation, EGFR amplification, BRAF V600E, MTAP loss, STK11 loss, MYC amplification, research marker D, E, and F, sex, CRISPR-library indicators, omics availability, screen batch, media serum concentration contrasts, and several secondary core-negative markers. In particular, the constructed research markers and signatures do not behave as main dependency predictors, and their high-subgroup marker associations mostly reflect the robust main marker effects rather than evidence of constructed-assay modification.\n\nCDKN2A loss is not robustly supported. Several core-negative discovery contrasts are near or above threshold, including R30, R48, and R95, but independent validation failed in high-MYC cells R143, high-aneuploidy cells R156, and core-negative high-aneuploidy cells R169. Direct CDKN2A interactions tested so far also do not establish modification. Invalid underpowered contrasts are design limitations, but they are not evidence of association. Therefore the best current conclusion is that CDKN2A loss is not a robustly associated dependency predictor in this dataset after validation and multiplicity.\n\nUnresolved uncertainty. The main unresolved scientific issue is PTEN-loss effect modification. Existing robust subgroup means show PTEN associations in many contexts, but direct interactions are mostly null or imprecise. The high-Wnt, high-AXL, fast-growth, lower-screen-quality, high-MYC, and slower-growth interactions remain useful follow-up targets. The MSI-high slower-growth attenuation signal is a secondary unresolved question. The four registered proposals are focused discovery interactions rather than new validations because validation capacity is exhausted: direct PTEN-loss interaction with high Wnt and high AXL within the core-negative population; a formally reversed PTEN-loss high-MYC attenuation proposal; and a formally reversed MSI-high slower-growth attenuation proposal. For PTEN proposals, the hypothesis is that the PTEN-loss association is stronger in the named context than in the complementary core-negative cells; direction -1 makes a positive signed interaction evidence for that stronger context effect. For reversed attenuation proposals, direction +1 makes a positive signed interaction evidence that the marker association is weaker in the named context. Future acceptance should require the interaction interval to support the claimed direction and be compatible with the 0.15 threshold; otherwise robust subgroup means should be reported as robustness only. Insufficient cell counts, if encountered, should be treated as design limitations rather than empirical nulls.\n\nFinal scientific status. The supplied dataset supports SMARCA4 loss and MSI-high as strong stronger-dependency markers, TP53 loss and KEAP1 loss as strong weaker-dependency markers, and PTEN loss as a moderate stronger-dependency marker. record.narrative:
No response deadlines or assessment requests are open, and independent validation capacity is exhausted. No new validation estimate changes an accepted claim, so the controller-maintained accepted set is unchanged.

Supported dataset-level findings. The threshold is 0.15 composite dependency-score units; more negative dependency_composite means stronger dependency. SMARCA4 loss is a strong stronger-dependency association, discovery H43/R40 = 0.804 [0.742, 0.867], independent validation R65 = 0.803 [0.712, 0.894]. MSI-high is a strong stronger-dependency association, H10/R10 = 0.775 [0.664, 0.885], validation R92 = 0.831 [0.668, 0.993]. TP53 loss is a strong weaker-dependency association, H11/R11 = 0.829 [0.767, 0.891], validation R78 = 0.771 [0.673, 0.868]. KEAP1 loss is a strong weaker-dependency association, H13/R7 = 0.810 [0.745, 0.875], validation R52 = 0.840 [0.754, 0.926]. PTEN loss is a moderate stronger-dependency association, H8/R8 = 0.239 [0.145, 0.332], validation R13 = 0.294 [0.149, 0.439]. PTEN robustness is visible in several contexts, including KEAP1-negative cells R39, TP53-negative cells R17, PIK3CA-negative cells R241, high-MYC subgroup R121/R130, and core-negative adeno or Wnt-score contexts, but these simple subgroup means are not established effect modification unless supported by an interaction interval.

Negative and non-robust findings. Broad categories of demographic, technical, media, omics-availability, lineage, research marker/signature contrasts, KRAS, EGFR amplification, BRAF, MYC amplification, MTAP, STK11, ERBB2, APC, NF1, RB1, BRCA2, SMAD4, and many secondary molecular predictors do not meet the threshold or direction requirement. CDKN2A loss is the best candidate but nonrobust: some core-negative discovery contrasts are near or above threshold, including R30, R48, and R95, but independent validation failed in high-MYC R143, high-aneuploidy R156, and core-negative high-aneuploidy R169. The overall CDKN2A point estimate R74 = 0.139 [0.065, 0.213] is below the threshold point, and after validation and multiplicity it is better reported as not robustly associated. Insufficient-cell contrasts are design limitations, not empirical nulls.

Interactions. No direct interaction has been accepted as meaningful effect modification. Many simple subgroup estimates for the four strong markers and PTEN are robust, but interaction contrasts generally have intervals that include zero and values below the practical threshold. Rejections against the stronger-context direction include PTEN high-AXL core-negative H231/R231 = -0.097 [-0.283, 0.089] and SMARCA4 high-MYC H132/R239 = -0.044 [-0.190, 0.103]. The most suggestive but still unresolved signals are PTEN attenuation in core-negative high-MYC cells, attenuation-signed H229/H232/R229 = 0.187 [0.031, 0.343], and the broader core-negative MYC threshold 5.0 interaction H236 = 0.173 [0.019, 0.327]. TP53-loss by high MYC H234 = 0.164 [0.034, 0.295] is also suggestive but imprecise. MSI-high slower-growth attenuation remains suggestive but not accepted, H225/R225 = -0.368 [-0.672, -0.064] against the stronger-context claim, with attenuation-signed interval 0.368 [0.064, 0.672], while the broader growth test H237 = 0.090 [-0.155, 0.335] is inconclusive. PTEN lower screen quality, fast growth, high-Wnt, stemness, hypoxia, and broader screen-quality interactions remain imprecise, for example R207, R216, and R217 have lower bounds below threshold.

Most informative next analysis. I registered three focused discovery direct interactions to address the main unresolved PTEN question: whether PTEN-loss is genuinely attenuated in TP53-loss cells, SMARCA4-loss cells, or high mutation-burden cells. These are attenuation tests with direction +1; a positive signed interaction would mean the PTEN stronger-dependency association is smaller in the named context than in its complement. Acceptance should require a signed interval supporting attenuation and compatible with the 0.15-unit threshold. Null or imprecise results would support additive robustness of the accepted PTEN association rather than accepted effect modification. All conclusions remain dataset-specific associations from the supplied dataset and do not establish causality, single-gene knockout mechanism, biological pathway interpretation, constructed-assay meaning, or generalizability beyond this dataset.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.

refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without

Research signatures (research_signature_a, research_signature_b, research_signature_c) are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers (research_marker_d_positive, research_marker_e_positive, research_marker_f_positive) are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
